## Description

A marine thecate dinoflagellate (40–54 µm), polyhedral, of the Californian red tides. Bioluminescent:
water deformation (a wave, an oar, a copepod's current) triggers within milliseconds a blue flash of
~0.1 s from the scintillons. Its capacity to glow is regulated by its circadian clock: at night it is
tens of times higher than by day, even in constant light.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: not seeded in the default drops (inoculate it from the Catalogue).
<!-- /GENERATED -->

[Bioluminescence](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md) on a shear response above ~10/s, with recharge and a
24-biological-hour clock (`circadian`, `day_capacity`). Helical swimming, phototaxis, cysts. An ellipse
(a squarer outline does not let the division close). Marine: not in the freshwater drops (it is
inoculated).

## Literature

- Hastings J.W., Sweeney B.M. (1957) PNAS 43: 804 (circadian rhythm of luminescence).
- Latz M.I., Bovard M., Kirk J.H. (2004) Biol. Bull. 207: 145 (flash triggered by shear).

## Not implemented yet

- Polyhedral theca not reproduced.
- No dark-field lens to see the flash on a dark background (roadmap C).
- No measured µmax; shear threshold, recharge and day capacity are orders of magnitude.

## Unique and shared mechanics

The only bioluminescent being; shares the shear response ([M2](../../mechanics/behavioural-responses.md)) with
*Halteria*, *Vorticella* and *Stentor*.
